1.explanation:
• rules/key-spacing.md explains the align: 'value' option and its multiline behavior (the root cause of the misalignment)  
• rules/object-curly-newline.md and rules/object-property-newline.md show how multiline object formatting is governed (affects when key-spacing kicks in)  
• rules/object-curly-spacing.md covers braces and spacing inside object literals within JSX  
• rules/indent.md is needed because indent interacts with JSX indentation and can mask or compound the misalignment  
• developer-guide/working-with-rules.md describes how ESLint fixers operate and where key-spacing injects whitespace—critical to tracing and reproducing the formatter bug
1.bug_scenario: When running ESLint’s --fix with the key-spacing rule set to { multiLine: { align: 'value' } } on JSX files, style prop objects inside JSX lose their tidy colon alignment. In the screenshots you can see that nested style objects—keys such as marginRight, color, opacity, fontSize, verticalAlign—are reformatted incorrectly across JSX props. The colon positions of the second and subsequent style props no longer line up with the first, creating an uneven, “ugly” look. The bug involves JSXAttribute nodes (style={...}), ObjectExpression formatting, and the key-spacing fixer’s alignment logic.
